parsedVerdict.reasoning: SettleClaim is an application-layer use case, and everything in it fits that role. Its constructor injects a domain repository (ClaimRepository) and an application port (CoverageSource). Both are dependency wiring from layers the application layer may use. The settle(claimId: string): Promise<number> signature uses only plain types. It takes no request, response or HTTP context, and it does not return one. The only thing it throws is DomainError, which the project declares itself in shared-kernel (domain layer). It is not an HTTP error from a web package. Its 'not-found' code is a domain error code, not an HTTP status code. The file does no direct I/O: loading and saving go through the repository interface, and coverage terms come through the port. It applies no framework decorators and extends no base classes. The domain logic stays on the aggregate (claim.settle, claim.decline). The use case only orchestrates: it decides to decline when no coverage terms are found. That is normal application-layer coordination. No candidate flags were raised.
